thread:
Samira: quick note from today's onboarding: GemmaX-4B -> int4 looks ok on short prompts but long-context completions degrade and produce headwise artifacts (repeats, odd phrasing) after ~5k. FP16 ppl 11.6, int4 16.4 beyond 5k. Anyone seen head permutation/alignment issues across runtimes? :thinking:
Ibrahim: Could be head-order or projector ordering mismatch between our exporter and runtime. Different libraries sometimes store heads in (num_heads, head_dim) vs flattened order. Did converter emit a head-permutation map?
Samira: Convert log shows: 
```
[INFO] projection_shape inferred: (4096,)
[WARN] head_order: unspecified, assuming contiguous
```
Model repo has notes "attention_layout: 'heads_first'" but exporter assumed "kv_last".
Noah: That'll shuffle Q/K/V matrices and corrupt rotary offsets per head. Also if vocab index casing differs (trainer used casefold), embeddings won't match. We saw both symptoms in earlier models.
Petra: Repro: I ran head_perm_probe: 
```
python tools/head_perm_probe.py --model converted/gemmax4b-int4/ --input tests/long_dialog.txt --maxlen 8192
```
Output: 
```
[WARN] head 2: perm mismatch detected (expected head_idx 2 -> got 5)
[WARN] head 3: phase_noise high @ pos 5120 (0.22 rad)
```
Ibrahim: Fixes to try: 1) exporter should preserve attention_layout and add explicit head_order map, 2) during convert, verify QKV shapes and raise if mismatch, 3) add a tokenization casing check (casefold vs lowercase vs none).
Samira: Also noticed tokenizer lowercasing discrepancies. Training used casefold (NFKC + casefold), converter pipeline used simple lower(). That created off-by-one in subword splits for acronyms and some CJK romanizations. Example: 
```
>>> tokenizer.tokenize("NASA Test")
['nasa', ' test']  # casefold ok
>>> tokenizer_converted.tokenize("NASA Test")
['n', 'AS', 'A', ' Test']  # bad split
```
Which then maps to different embedding indices.
Yuki: For quant, I tested symmetric vs asymmetric per-head. Asymmetric per-channel (gptq) kept downstream ROUGE within 1 pt; symmetric global quant gave larger regressions. Commands used: 
```
python tools/convert.py --src gemmax4b/ --dst converted/gemmax4b-int4-qgt/ --quant gptq --preserve-perhead --quant-mode asymmetric
```
That plus correct head_order reduced ppl to 12.8 longctx.
Noah: I added a small CI check: `head_perm_probe.py` compares expected head indices (from model config) to actual weight layout and fails onboarding if mismatch. Also added tokenization roundtrip with casefold.
Infra Bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/1733333333/gemmax-convert-logs.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Petra: After swapping head order and using asymmetric gptq + casefold normalization, summarization BLEU/ROUGE recovered ~0.8 pts versus fp16; still slight delta but acceptable for staging. We should run full eval before promoting.
Ibrahim: Action items: 1) Patch exporter to emit attention_layout and head_map (PR in review), 2) Update convert.py to verify QKV shapes and support explicit head_order flag, 3) Make onboarding tokenizer pipeline run NFKC+casefold by default for models tagged with 'casefold' training metadata, 4) Add head_perm_probe to onboarding CI and warn if perm mismatch or phase_noise >0.05 rad.
Samira: I'll file tickets RED-7051 (exporter head_map), RED-7052 (convert QKV verification), RED-7053 (tokenizer casefold default), RED-7054 (head_perm_probe on CI).
Yuki: One more note: some downstream evals (coding datasets) show weird tokenization on camelCase identifiers when casefold is applied; add a flag to skip casefold for code-like models.
Noah: Good call. We'll gate casefold by model metadata (training_domain: 'natural' vs 'code').
